Register of Electors: 
The Electoral Reform Act 2022 introduced the modernisation of the Electoral Register, 
which allows for a rolling or continually updating register.  This is more convenient for 
electors as they can register or update their details at any time, other than the closing 
date before a polling day (14 days).  Voters go to checktheregister.ie if they want to check 
if they are registered to vote or check or update their details.   
 
The Franchise Team collaborated with St Catherine’s Community Services Centre, Carlow 
to host a National Voter Registration Day Event on Thursday 30th April 2026.  At the event 
Carlow Co Council was on hand to provide guidance, answer queries and support anyone 
who needed assistance registering to vote or checking and updating their registration 
details.  
 
Register of Electors National Data Cleansing Project 
The Franchise Team are actively participating in a National Data Cleansing Project. For 
the month of May, the Franchise Team continued reviewing the register and are in the 
process of facilitating communication to electors who need to update their details on the 
register of electors.  The changes to the Register for the month of May included the

Rás Tailteann 2026  
The Ra s Tailteann returned to Carlow in May 2026. On Saturday 23rd May Stage four 
started in Carlow and finished in Wicklow.  On Sunday 24th May the final stage started in 
Carlow, crossing the plains of Carlow and onto Kildare.  Event registration and the 
starting point took place at County Buildings, Athy Road, Carlow and was facilitated by 
Carlow Co Council.  The race entourage stayed in Carlow town on 22nd and 23rd May. 
 
Carlow Town has hosted stages of the international cycling stage race in previous years, 
including 2013, 2015 and 2018. 
 
 
Performance Indicators: 
The National Oversight & Audit Committee ‘NOAC’ gathers and validates data on local 
authority performance indicators annually.  The 2025 data collection will inform NOAC’s 
performance indicator report.  The data submission date was Friday, 17th April 2026.  
Carlow Co. Council was selected for a random evaluation process which was facilitated by 
Corporate Services on 27th May.   The NOAC Report will be published Q4 2026.

LEO ‘Lunch & Learn’ Outreach events 
The Local Enterprise Office held a series of ‘lunch and learn’ outreach events in 
May to introduce LEO services to the business community. Events took place in 
each Municipal District with almost 70 business owners attending. 
   
Lean Educational Visit 
13 Carlow businesses participated in a Local Enterprise Office educational trip to 
Adman Steel Sheds in Wexford, a nationally recognised model of best practice in 
the use of lean processes in business.  
 
Management Development Programme in Hacketstown  
The Local Enterprise Office, in partnership with South East Technological 
University, announced the launch of ‘Hub Grow’ a management development 
programme focussing on business innovation. The programme will commence in 
June and will be delivered in Station House, Hacketstown.  
 
Evaluations & Approvals Committee 
A meeting of the Local Enterprise Office Evaluations & Approvals Committee was 
held in May. €69,404 in grant aid was approved to 3 applicants.  
 
Student Enterprise Programme 
County Carlow was represented by 3 student groups at the National Final for the 
Student Enterprise Programme: 2 from Coláiste Eoin, Hacketstown (Junior and 
Senior Category) and 1 from Tullow Community College (Intermediate Category).

workshop with Simone Foster of Optimum Results. This practical course was 
designed to teach business owners and managers how to adopt Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) into their business in a responsible way, to teach them how to use 
accurate prompts and ultimately to help them optimise their business processes.

Catalyst HQ – SMART Regions 
The project has moved into the delivery phase, with weekly project meetings now 
underway to progress design, governance, and implementation milestones. The tender 
will be advertised in June 2026.   
Catalyst HQ will be delivered in partnership with Southeast Catalyst Innovation 
Company CLG. Southeast Catalyst Innovation Company CLG, trading as Catalyst HQ, is 
co-funded by the Government of Ireland and the European Union through the ERDF 
Southern, Eastern and Midland Regional Programme 2021–2027.   
The Sorting House – Borris 
The tender pack is being finalized for the project and will be advertised in June 2026.  
 
Creative Europe – EU Craft Work 4.0 ALL 
The EU Craft project is ongoing with regular weekly communications focused on 
monitoring and reviewing key performance metrics. A Creative Spark Fab Lab was held 
on 30th April 2026 with 12 participants in association with the Library Service. A 
workshop was held in Louth as part of our partnership with Louth County Council.   
 
Participants from Ireland will visit Greece on the 2nd – 5th June as part of the Craftwork 
4.0 All project with Borris Lace travelling to deliver workshops.  
 
Erasmus + KA2 - Hands Across Generations  
Carlow Library Service co-ordinated the delivery of the development of a sustainability 
training module as part of the programme which will be delivered later in the year. An 
inter regional meeting was held on the 2nd – 5th June 2026 in Greece.  The feedback for 
the first progress report was received with some recommendations to be actioned.  
 
Erasmus + KA2 - Digi-Text  
The Digi Text project with Kilkis Chamber (Greece) was progressed during the month. 
Representatives from Greece will visit Carlow between 6th – 10th July 2026 for a 
programme development session. Representatives from Ireland visited Greece on the 
2nd-5th June 2026.  Applications were open until the 7th May for interested crafters to 
attend. 13 applications were received and 6 people were selected.   
 
Carlow- Luxembourg 
A series of meetings was progressed for the Economic Development programme for 
Carlow and Luxembourg during the EU Presidency.   
 
COSME – Slow Tourism 
An application was developed for the EU Fund COSME in respect of a proposed Slow 
Tourism project in partnership with a series of EU Partners. A decision is expected in 
October.

Forward Planning 
 
Update on Development Plan  
 
Variation No. 3 of the Carlow County Development Plan 2022-2028 to incorporate the 
draft and final Tullow District Town Plan 2026 was formally approved by the Elected 
Members at the full Council Meeting on 11th May 2026 and becomes effective immediately 
 
Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy 
The Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy (RSES) for the Southern Region is currently 
under review. The Issues Paper was published on the 26/3/26 and identifies key 
strategic themes encompassing creating a liveable region, a green region, a creative and 
innovative region.  The public consultation period closed on 22/5/26. Carlow County 
Council as a key stakeholder in the process has made a formal submission to the process. 
The content of the submission is available for public viewing at this link: Review of the 
Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy for the Southern Region (RSES) | Southern 
Regional Assembly's Consultation Portal Following consideration of submissions a 
Directors Report will be prepared for consideration by the members of the regional 
assembly followed by preparation of the Draft RSES at which time further consultation 
will take place.  
 
Given the strategic position of Carlow Town within two regional assembly areas Carlow 
County Council has also made a submission to the Eastern and Midlands Regional 
Assembly which can be accessed at this link: Pre-DRAFT RSES Public Consultation - 
Strategic Issues Paper | Eastern and Midland Regional Assembly's Consultation Portal.

District Heating Feasibility Study   
Carlow County Council have undertaken a District Heating Feasibility Study in Carlow 
Town  Decarbonising Zone.  This project involves the delivery of a district heating 
feasibility study for Carlow Town, led by Carlow County Council in collaboration with 
SEAI under the Pathfinder Programme.  It aims to evaluate the technical, financial, 
environmental and planning viability of establishing a district heating network within the 
Carlow Decarbonisation Zone, building on initial pre-feasibility findings that highlight 
strong potential due to the town’s compact layout, concentrated heat demand, and 
available renewable energy sources such as geothermal heat. The expected outcomes of 
the project include the identification of the most suitable areas and anchor clients for 
network development, a detailed heat demand and supply assessment, appraisal of viable 
heat source options, and the preparation of an evidence-based business case with 
indicative costs, risks and governance structures, ultimately providing a clear roadmap 
for the potential implementation of a low-carbon district heating system in Carlow.
